shots.evidence: Momentum is mass times velocity, $p=mv$. A 2 kg ball moving at 5 m/s has a momentum magnitude of 10 kg m/s.
shots.ball: A 2 kg ball moves at 5 m/s. What is the magnitude of its momentum?
shots.hint: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity, so multiply the mass by the speed.
shots.explanation: The formula is $p=mv$. Substituting gives $p = 2\ \text{kg} \times 5\ \text{m/s} = 10\ \text{kg m/s}$. The unit kilogram metre per second comes from multiplying kilograms by metres per second.

shots.evidence: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion, $E_k=\frac{1}{2}mv^2$. A 2 kg ball travelling at 3 m/s has 9 J of kinetic energy.
shots.ball: A 2 kg ball moves at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
shots.hint: Kinetic energy equals one half times the mass times the square of the speed.
shots.explanation: The formula is $E_k=\frac{1}{2}mv^2$. Substituting gives $E_k = \frac{1}{2} \times 2\ \text{kg} \times (3\ \text{m/s})^2 = 9\ \text{J}$, because the squared speed is $9\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}^2$.

shots.evidence: Average velocity is displacement divided by elapsed time, $v=\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}$. Travelling 12 m east in 4 s gives an average velocity of 3 m/s east.
shots.ball: A cart travels 12 m east in 4 s along a straight line. What is its average velocity?
shots.hint: Average velocity is displacement divided by the elapsed time.
shots.explanation: The formula is $v=\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}$. Substituting gives $v = \frac{12\ \text{m}}{4\ \text{s}} = 3\ \text{m/s}$ directed east, the same direction as the displacement.

shots.evidence: The change in gravitational potential energy is $\Delta E_p=mg\Delta h$. Raising a 2 kg mass by 3 m with $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ increases its potential energy by 60 J.
shots.ball: A 2 kg object rises 3 m, with $g = 10\ \text{m/s}^2$. How much does its gravitational potential energy change?
shots.hint: Compute the mass times gravitational acceleration times the height change.
shots.explanation: The change in gravitational potential energy is $\Delta E_p = mgh$. Substituting gives $\Delta E_p = 2\ \text{kg} \times 10\ \text{m/s}^2 \times 3\ \text{m} = 60\ \text{J}$, and it is an increase because the object rises.
